weaknesses: Negative test cases incorrectly assert that invalid values are accepted; they should assert rejection or error.
Oracle assertions for negative cases are not grounded; they should check for error messages or state changes.
The test suite does not verify that the GUI control actually restricts input to the specified range; it only sets values.
Boundary tests use only single boundary values; they should also test values just inside the boundary (e.g., 6, 29) to ensure correct handling.
The alarm test for relief valve opens does not verify that the alarm is triggered only when flow increases unexpectedly; it lacks a control scenario where flow is normal.

artifact:
Feature: Alarm Threshold Settings and Detection
  As a user of the GUI
  I want to set thresholds for alarms
  So that I can configure the system to alert me appropriately

  @RW-SW-144
  Scenario: GUI has a control for setting the threshold for HIGH RR alarm
    Given the GUI is displayed
    Then the HIGH RR alarm threshold control is visible

  @RW-SW-145
  Scenario Outline: The control for setting the threshold for HIGH RR alarm allows setting values between 5-30 in increments of 1
    Given the HIGH RR alarm threshold control is visible
    When I set the threshold to <value>
    Then the HIGH RR alarm threshold is set to <value>
    Examples:
      | value |
      | 5     |
      | 15    |
      | 30    |
      | 4     | # invalid
      | 31    | # invalid

  @RW-SW-146
  Scenario: GUI has a control for setting the threshold for LOW RR alarm
    Given the GUI is displayed
    Then the LOW RR alarm threshold control is visible

  @RW-SW-147
  Scenario Outline: The control for setting the threshold for LOW RR alarm allows setting values between 5-30 in increments of 1
    Given the LOW RR alarm threshold control is visible
    When I set the threshold to <value>
    Then the LOW RR alarm threshold is set to <value>
    Examples:
      | value |
      | 5     |
      | 15    |
      | 30    |
      | 4     | # invalid
      | 31    | # invalid

  @RW-SW-148
  Scenario: GUI has a control for setting the threshold for the apnea alarm
    Given the GUI is displayed
    Then the apnea alarm threshold control is visible

  @RW-SW-149
  Scenario Outline: The control for setting the threshold for the apnea alarm allows setting values between 1-30 seconds in increments of 1s
    Given the apnea alarm threshold control is visible
    When I set the threshold to <value> seconds
    Then the apnea alarm threshold is set to <value> seconds
    Examples:
      | value |
      | 1     |
      | 15    |
      | 30    |
      | 0     | # invalid
      | 31    | # invalid

  @RW-SW-158
  Scenario: Alarm when relief valve opens based on unexpected increase in flow
    Given the system is monitoring flow
    When there is an unexpected increase in flow
    Then the relief valve opens alarm is triggered
